slots.label: ECO Elective or other Approved Course
ECO Elective or other Approved Course

notes.text: Students are urged to consider enrolling in ECO 488 - Internship in Economics. Registration requires an internship offer (through the Career Center or otherwise) and permission of a faculty member; the permission and Career Center arrangement must be made before the start of the semester. The academic component runs alongside the work component.

Independent research (ECO 487) should be formulated with the supervising faculty member before the start of the semester in which it is taken. Credit is variable (about four hours per week per credit).
Economics is a quantitative social science. Students planning graduate study or careers using economics should take additional mathematics and applied mathematics courses.
Students who need to take MAP 103 cannot take ECO 110 or ECO 111 in their first semester of freshman year and must adjust their schedule.

Honors in Economics is available. Requirements include a 3.5 GPA in the five required courses with no less than a B in any one, a 3.50 GPA in five upper-division economics electives, six credits in economics at the 400 level, and an honors thesis evaluated by the Undergraduate Committee. The honors program is not evaluated here.
Double majors must fulfill the Economics upper-division writing requirement in addition to their other major's upper-division writing requirement.

Upper-division writing should generally be completed in the senior year, after most upper-division major requirements are done. ECO 459 may be used with a paper from another upper-division class only in exceptional cases, with instructor and student agreement, and with registration for ECO 459 in the same semester.
Students may consider Second Majors and Minors in Applied Mathematics and Statistics (AMS), Business (BUS, major only), and Computer Science (CSE).
